reason: The hypothesis relies on the premise that coherent nanoprecipitates strengthen without harming magnetic properties, which is directly supported by E1 for a CoFeNiTaAl HEA. However, E1 and E2 provide no evidence that this mechanism applies to MnNiSi-based alloys, that the magnetocaloric effect behaves like soft magnetic properties, or that the proposed annealing parameters will produce the required precipitates in this specific material system.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates (<15 nm) can strengthen an alloy while only marginally increasing coercivity.
The strengthening mechanism is dislocation blocking by coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherency of precipitates minimizes magnetic domain wall pinning, preserving soft magnetic properties.
The magnetocaloric effect (ΔS) is analogous to soft magnetic properties and will be similarly preserved by coherent precipitates.
A specific annealing treatment (700°C, 30 min) can produce the required coherent nanoprecipitate distribution in MnNiSi-based alloys.
